$comment: Pins the values a wrong TYPE or a wrong ENUM would silently mis-render. Enums: a wrong clusterProfile renders the dev topology and the drift hook cannot catch it. Booleans: Helm's `not`/`and`/`or`/`ternary` are strict — a knob set to 0 or "true" aborts the render with 'wrong type for value; expected bool; got int64', so the type is checked up front instead. Everything else stays permissive (no additionalProperties:false anywhere) — Helm injects `global`, and future tiers add keys. Every boolean leaf of values.yaml is typed here; scripts/ci/values-schema-bools-check.py fails the build when a new one is added without a matching constraint.

instances.description: Instance count for this data tier. null (the default) = the cluster profile's count (clusterProfileInstances); an explicit integer wins over the profile.
Instance count for this data tier. null (the default) = the cluster profile's count (clusterProfileInstances); an explicit integer wins over the profile.

replicas.description: Pod count for this service. null (the default) = the cluster profile's count (clusterProfileReplicas), or 1 when the profile has no entry; an explicit integer — including 0, the scale-off — wins over the profile.

port.description: The port the container listens on and every piece of plumbing (Service targetPort, NetworkPolicy, probes) dials. The chart also sets the process's own port (PORT, or --port for redis), so an override moves the LISTENER too. ClamAV is the exception the render enforces: clamd takes its port from clamd.conf, so only 3310 is accepted.

progressDeadlineSeconds.description: Per-service override of global.progressDeadlineSeconds \u2014 the Deployment's progress window in seconds. Optional: not declared in values.yaml, because a concrete value there would always be present \u2014 an overlay can set the key, never remove it \u2014 and the template reads the service key before the chart-wide one, which would make the global knob inert. A value below 1 second is rejected by the render.

clusterProfileInstances.description: clusterProfile-driven instance counts for the data tier (Keycloak, Postgres). An explicit data.<tier>.instances wins over these.

clusterProfileReplicas.description: clusterProfile-driven replica overrides. The order is the EXPLICIT value, then the profile, then 1: `services.<svc>.replicas` wins over this map when it is set (null by default = the profile applies).

global.$comment: Closed block: every key the templates read through the captured $global is typed, and unknown keys are REJECTED at render (Helm would otherwise accept a typo'd key as nil — e.g. `imagePullSecret` for `imagePullSecrets`, read from 13 sites — and every pod would ImagePullBackOff in the cluster with no schema error naming the key). toolingArch and kubeletToolsMirror additionally constrain shapes the render interpolates into a shell. The block coalesces wholesale into subcharts (gateway-helm): verified it ships no schema and reads no global.* key, so closing here cannot reject a key it consumes.

imageRegistry.description: Optional registry prefix that WINS over the top-level imageRegistry when set (the factory and the migrations Job read it first); empty = the top-level imageRegistry applies. Exists for operators following the Helm global.* convention — the chart's own overlays set the top-level key.

progressDeadlineSeconds.description: The progress deadline every Deployment the chart renders carries. Kubernetes defaults spec.progressDeadlineSeconds to 600s and that clock starts when the DEPLOYMENT is created, not when the pod runs: on a first install the pod is created minutes later (multi-GB images still pulling) and inherits only what is left of the window. Past it the Deployment reports ProgressDeadlineExceeded, Helm declares the release failed and uninstalls it, deleting the resources the next attempt needs. Per-service override: services.<svc>.progressDeadlineSeconds. An explicit null clears the knob back to the template default.

items.description: A pull-credential Secret reference ({name: <Secret>}) wired into every service pod's spec.imagePullSecrets.

imagePullSecrets.description: Pull credentials for a registry that requires authentication — only about the PULL CREDENTIALS; the registry images are pulled FROM is the top-level imageRegistry.

toolingArch.description: Forces the kubectl binary architecture the tools-init container downloads; empty = detect from uname -m. Constrained to the values the download URL accepts — the value is interpolated into the init container's shell, so anything outside the enum is rejected at render, not executed.

toolingImageRegistry.description: Registry for Helm hook Jobs and test pods that pull public Docker Hub images (alpine, python, busybox); empty = docker.io. Separate from the top-level imageRegistry, which scopes service images to the GitLab Container Registry.

kubeletToolsMirror.description: Internal mirror for the kubectl download: [http[s]://]host[:port 1-65535][/multi/segment/prefix] — the scheme is optional and LOWERCASE-only (busybox wget rejects mixed-case schemes; scheme-less makes wget use plain HTTP), /release/... is appended (the binary is checksum-verified against a sha256 pinned in the chart — the mirror serves the binary only), and the prefix may carry multiple path segments (the Nexus/Artifactory repository topology). No trailing slash (it would double the appended path's leading slash on strict routers). The host admits a colon only before a numeric port in the 1-65535 range, and the scheme only http(s): the value is interpolated into the tools-init container's shell inside double quotes, and any other shape (file://, https:mirror, :99999, shell metacharacters) is rejected at render.

imagePullPolicy.description: Global pull-policy override for the service images; empty = follows the tag (mutable tags pull Always, pinned tags IfNotPresent), and a per-service services.<svc>.image.pullPolicy beats both.

okf.description: The OKF knowledge-frame tier. Dark by default — mirrors Compose's OKF_ENABLED=0.
